newsitem.title: USA: U.S. high-grade debt sells, some junk challenged.
newsitem.headline: U.S. high-grade debt sells, some junk challenged.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond issuance totaling more than $1.0 billion revealed still-strong investor cravings for high-grade bonds on Wednesday, while secondary spreads sat unchanged, dealers said.

The same could not be said for high-yield bonds, however, with a $300 million issue from WinStar Communications Inc called a "workout" situation. The issue, restructured to eliminate a $150 million 10-year senior subordinated deferred interest tranche and hike price talk elsewhere, is now expected to price on Thursday.
Street sources said the deal was slated for Wednesday.
Some players noted a more cautious market for the more speculative grade bonds has upended deals such as Teleport Communications Group, WinStar and the wireless British telephone company Ionica Plc.

"The WinStar and Ionica are not considered the tier 1 or better quality names, so they would be a hard sales in any market," said John Bianchi, managing director of Smith Barney Inc's high-yield funds.
Bianchi said he is willing to give up higher yield of such lower quality issues (WinStar was rated CCC-plus by Standard & Poor's in return for the lower spread risk of a BB paper.
Ionica is also expected to price on Thursday.
Elsewhere, two other high-yield deals found enough demand to prompt increases in size before pricing on Wednesday.

Hollinger International Publishing sold $550 million in notes, up from $400 million, in two tranches through Merrill Lynch & Co. The deal included $260 million 8-5/8 percent Ba3/BB-plus senior notes due 2005 to yield 212.5 basis points over Treasuries and $290 million 9-1/4 percent 10-year B1/BB-minus senior subordinated notes to yield 275 basis points over the curve.
Also Nortek Inc priced $175 million, up from $150 million, 10-year Ba3/B-plus senior notes as 9-1/4s to yield 275 basis points over the curve via Bear, Stearns & Co.
Some high-grade issues were also increased in size, including $550 million in two-tranche debt from Honeywell Inc via lead manager J.P. Morgan Securities Inc.

The issue included $200 million 6-3/4 percent five-year notes priced to yield 34 basis points over the curve and $350 million seven percent 10-year notes priced to yield 50 basis points over. Both tranches are rated A2/single-A.

Dave Olsen, vice president of J.P. Morgan's debt capital group, said while corporate demand was perhaps not as fervent as seen two weeks ago, the increase in the 10-year tranche from $200 million to $350 million proved depth to the market.

"Getting more than half a billion (dollars) for a real bread and butter corporate name gave the best indication that there is a lot of strength left in the investor community," said Olsen. "Particularly for more infrequent issuers."
Other investment grade issues were:
-- 360 Communications Co's $200 million Ba1/BBB-minus 7.60 percent notes due 2009, priced to yield 103 basis points over the Treasury curve via Salomon Brothers.
-- Westvaco Corp's $150 million A1/single-A 7.65 percent 30-year debentures priced to yield 77 basis points over the Treasury bond.
Corporate bond spreads in the secondary were mostly unchanged, traders said, with most focus geared toward the new issue slate.
The T-bond closed down 11/32 to yield 6.88 percent.
